title: Lateral Move Success Kit — 21-day Activation Sprint (Playbook & Checklists)
content:
Purpose and scope:

This playbook is a compact, practical kit for orchestrating lateral moves (internal transfers) into technical and product-facing roles at Redwood Inference. It is designed around a 21-day activation sprint to get the transferring employee to a baseline of independent contribution while minimizing operational risk. This is intentionally lightweight — aimed at hiring managers, cross-functional partners, and the people-ops partner who owns the move.

Objective:
- Deliver a repeatable 21-day plan to accelerate lateral hires into new roles with clear responsibilities, KT (knowledge transfer), and measurable outcomes.
- Reduce time-to-first-meaningful-change while protecting service continuity and minimizing shadowing burden on teams.

When to use this kit:
- Lateral moves where the hire is internal (existing Redwood employee) and needs a structured rapid ramp (role change across teams, e.g., infra -> serving-runtime or product -> engineering).
- Not intended for junior/entry hires or full-scale cross-discipline retraining (use standard 60–120 day onboarding variants).

Primary owners / stakeholders:
- People Ops sponsor: owns the checklist and approvals (Sofia Martinez)
- Receiving manager: role owner for the 21-day plan and success criteria
- Originating manager: ensures handoff and provides role context
- Buddy / mentor: assigned (preferably a peer IC) for day-to-day questions
- SRE/Platform contact: if role touches infra or private deployments

Pre-move checklist (to be completed before Day 0) — must be greenlined before transfer:
1) Acceptance & role brief: written role description and three 30/60/90 outcomes from receiving manager.
2) Access inventory: list of required systems, with owners and approval steps (AWS, GCP, private cluster, GitHub org, Redwood Console).
3) Workspace & infra: dev environment and any hardware allocation confirmed (if relevant).
4) Compliance & security signoffs: training, NDA extensions, KMS access requests filed.
5) Knowledge transfer window: originate manager commits 2 half-days for synchronous KT in the first 7 days.

Kickoff (Day 0 — 0.5 day)
- 30–60 minute welcome call: receiving manager, buddy, people-ops sponsor. Set expectations and the 21-day sprint plan.
- Slack intro post template (copyable):
  "Please welcome [Name] who is joining [Team] from [Origin team]! First day is today — they’ll be focused on getting up to speed on [area]. Please ping their buddy @buddy for questions."
- Confirm calendar blocks for daily stand catch-ups for first 10 business days (15 minutes).

21-day activation breakdown (high-level):
Days 1–3: Orientation & essential access
- Confirm all access (read/write where appropriate).
- Pair with buddy to run dev environment bootcamp: run local tests, lint, and one small read-only query against a staging endpoint.
- Deliverable: submit a short "smoke test" note verifying environment and two quick tickets observed in the codebase.

Days 4–7: Focused KT & shadowing
- Synchronous KT sessions with originating manager (2x 90m) covering context, recurring work, and key architecture diagrams.
- Shadow the buddy during a real triage or deploy window.
- Deliverable: create a "Role context" note in team wiki summarizing 5 things they would change and 3 questions to explore.

Days 8–14: Small independent loop & micro-ownership
- Owner a small bug or enhancement (<= 3 days) with paired review. End-to-end: branch, PR, review, staging validation, and deployment verification.
- Introduce the new hire to the primary observability dashboards (Console traces, token cost dashboards) and cost/tagging guidance.
- Deliverable: merged PR + retrospective note on what was learned and what blockers remain.

Days 15–21: Consolidation, process handoff, and roadmap alignment
- Take ownership of a lightweight operational task (on-call doc update, runbook fix, dashboard tweak) and present to team at end-of-week demo.
- Define 30/60/90 goals with receiving manager and log into performance tracker (shared doc).
- Deliverable: 21-day retro (what worked/what didn’t) and a prioritized 30-day backlog.

Interview rubric adjustments for lateral moves (for final interview / role fit calibration) — guidance for hiring managers and interviewers:
- Emphasize context transferability rather than pure syntax knowledge: evaluate ability to learn systems and reason about tradeoffs.
- Evidence anchors: ask for 1 specific example of systems ownership, 1 example of cross-team collaboration, and 1 learning story where they onboarded or shifted domain.
- Scoring: Communication (0–3), Domain Transfer (0–3), Autonomy (0–2), Impact orientation (0–2). Minimum pass threshold: 6/10 with no zero in Communication or Autonomy.

Mentor/buddy playbook (recommended lightweight charter) — 4 responsibilities:
1) Daily sync first 10 business days (15m) to unblock and orient.
2) Review PRs quickly (24–48h SLA) for any assigned tickets.
3) Provide two short shadowing sessions during week 1.
4) Check-in at day 21 to agree next steps and future pairing pattern.

Knowledge transfer templates (use as quick prompts during KT sessions):
- "I wish I knew this on day 1" — 5 bullets.
- "Hidden dependencies" — repo/services that often break this flow.
- "Emergency playbook" — top 3 remediation steps for the most common incident.

Risk mitigation & escalation plan:
- If environment access is not granted by Day 3, escalate to people-ops sponsor and IT owner; block timeout = 72 hours.
- If no merged PR or measurable progress by Day 14, run a mid-sprint calibration with receiving manager + people-ops + originating manager to adjust scope.

Success metrics (to be recorded in the People Ops transfer tracker):
- Environment green (boolean) by Day 3.
- First merged PR by Day 14 (yes/no and description).
- Buddy NPS-style pulse at Day 10 (scale 1–5).
- Receiving manager assessment at Day 21: Ready for independent work (Yes/No) + qualitative note.

Templates / copyable snippets
- Day 0 Slack intro (see above).
- Weekly sponsor update (two sentences):
  "Progress update: [Name] completed environment setup and merged initial PR. Risks: [access / KT gap]. Next steps: [short backlog]."

Lightweight accountability checklist (tick boxes)
- [ ] Role brief + 30/60/90 outcomes agreed (pre-move)
- [ ] Access inventory created + requests filed (pre-move)
- [ ] Buddy assigned (pre-move)
- [ ] Kickoff call held (Day 0)
- [ ] Environment smoke test posted (Day 3)
- [ ] KT sessions scheduled and completed (Day 7)
- [ ] First PR merged (Day 14)
- [ ] 21-day retro completed (Day 21)

Common pitfalls and advice (from managers):
- Don’t overload with long-running projects in first 21 days — focus on ship-small, learn-fast cycles.
- Avoid assuming tech parity between teams; always validate stack differences by walking through a simple end-to-end flow.
- Keep a narrow first-sprint scope; success breeds confidence and lowers friction for later ramp tasks.

Appendix: Quick links and artifact pointers
- Example 21-day retro template (copy into team wiki).
- People Ops transfer tracker (link): confluence:INTERNAL-TRF-21
- Relevant onboarding playbooks: security onboarding, console access guide.

Notes / open questions (items people-ops should finalize):
- Should people-ops auto-assign a mentor pool for cross-pool moves? (proposal pending)
- Decide whether lateral moves into private-deployments require additional hardware shadowing windows beyond the 21 days.

Owners & next steps:
- People Ops (Sofia Martinez): finalize checklists and publish canonical template in team wiki (target: 2025-11-28).
- Receiving managers: start using this playbook for next three lateral moves and share feedback in the people-ops retro channel.

End of playbook.
